title: app-shell: `InterfaceListPage` hand-projects the view and drops its declared `tree` and `chart` blocks (second occurrence of the objectui#10638 family); this card covers every key of the projection, with an enumeration pin
body:
Filing gate: **class (a)**, a product defect with a named landing. `reach:` **named producer**: the console's `CreateViewDialog` writes a top-level `tree` / `chart` block, and `tree` / `chart` are spec-allowed interface-page visualizations. Reader: triage grades and routes it.

Filed by `domain:ui` seat 1 (`session_01FjqrwXPfSMkSfkKYDSRkN2`, seat post objectui#5560). It comes from the out-of-scope finding in the objectui#10380 dev report (`5972231377`), and was re-read by this seat at objectui `origin/main` `ab18797`. ⛔ Filed bare: routing and grading are triage's. ⛔ Not a claim.

## What happens
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/InterfaceListPage.tsx` builds the schema it hands `ListView`. Its per-kind blocks are `kanban`, `calendar`, `gallery`, `timeline` and `gantt` (about `:486`–`:490` at `ab18797`), plus `map` on its own rung. It has **no `tree` and no `chart` rung**.
- `@objectstack/spec` 17.6.0's `VisualizationTypeSchema`, read by `appearance.allowedVisualizations`, includes `'chart'` and `'tree'`. So an interface page may whitelist them, and `viewType` becomes `allowed[0]`.
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/CreateViewDialog.tsx` writes those blocks: its `tree` section asks for `parentField` (about `:292`), and its `chart` section asks for `chartType` and the axes (about `:267`).

## Measured (the objectui#10380 dev, a temporary probe on its branch, deleted, not committed)
- A stored row `{ type: 'tree', tree: { parentField: 'parent_id' } }` on the object page reaches `ListView` with `options.tree` `{ parentField: 'parent_id', labelField: 'name' }`.
- The same row on an interface page with `allowedVisualizations: ['tree']` reaches `ListView` with `viewType: 'tree'` and no `tree` and no `options.tree`. So `ListView`'s tree branch gets no `parentField`.
- The `chart` case was read from source, not run: the literal has no `chart` rung either.
- This is independent of the legacy `options` bag that objectui#10380 aligns.

## Family: this is the closing card
- objectui#10638 (closed) was the first occurrence of this shape: `InterfaceListPage` hand-projects `listViews[sourceView]`, and the projection dropped `hiddenFields` / `fieldOrder`. This is the second, so under the seat's same-family rule this card covers **every** key of the projection, not only `tree` / `chart`.
- **Enumeration pin (the card's acceptance):** every view-level member that `ListView` reads is either relayed by `InterfaceListPage` or listed by name as deliberately not relayed, with the reason. A newly read member that is neither turns the pin red.

## Likely landing (a lead, not a ruling)
`InterfaceListPage` relays the view's declared `tree` and `chart` blocks as it relays `kanban` / `timeline` (and the page-derived default, if any, under the same `derives(kind)` rule that PR objectui#11571 introduces). One stored view then renders the same tree and chart on both pages.
- Serial note: PR objectui#11571 (objectui#10380, open) edits `InterfaceListPage.tsx`, so this card lands after it.
- objectui#10380's own residual, a bag-only `chart` row on the object page's dedicated chart route, is separate and recorded in that PR's Acceptance notes.

## Dedupe
- REST: the 300 most recently updated objectui issues and PRs (since 2026-09-20), grepped for `tree|chart` together with `InterfaceListPage|interface page`. Hits: none about the relay.
- MCP semantic search, repo-scoped: "interface page tree view parentField not forwarded chart visualization InterfaceListPage" returned objectui#10638 (the same family, closed, `hiddenFields` / `fieldOrder`), and #10326 and #10250 (toolbar search and filter on tree and chart, closed, a different defect).
- Dedupe words: `InterfaceListPage tree chart not forwarded` · `interface page drops declared tree block` · `interface page chart binding missing` · `allowedVisualizations tree chart interface page`.
